messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: use multicore within simulateData
parts:
On 07/19/2015 12:36 PM, et wrote:
> dear lavaan users,
> has anybody of you ever tried to use multicore=TRUE (snow or multicore)
> within the simulateData function in lavaan? it does't work within my
> simulation... or is there any better option within snowfall maybe to use
> all processor cores?

I am not sure what you try to accomplish here. The function
simulateData() itself has no support for multicore=TRUE, in the sense
that what happens within simulateData() can not (easily) be
parallelized. It is supposed to generate data once.

But you can of course write your own function, (say, oneRun()), that
calls simulateData() to generate the data, fits the model, and extracts
the information you need, and call this with mcapply.

You can also try the simsem package.

Yves.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: use multicore within simulateData
parts: i am not sure what "list" argument i should put into the mclapply function, because later i want to give names to the covariance matrices via lapply and then it doesn't work any more...

The "list" could be the replication number.  If you want 500 replications, then your list could be the vector 1:500, or it could be a vector of RNG-seeds.

What you want to do is create a function that returns the data your need for a single replication.  Here is an example:

daten.erzeugen <- function(x, N, pop) {
  myCov <- simulateData(model = pop, sample.nobs = N, seed = x,
auto.fix.first = FALSE, return.type = "cov")

rownames(myCov) <- paste0("x", 1:20)
  colnames(myCov) <- paste0("x", 1:20)
  myCov
}

pop.model1 <- "..."
nReps <- 500
set.seed(123)
seeds <- sample(1000000:9999999, size = nReps)
COV.1000 <- lapply(seeds, daten.erzeugen, N = 1000, pop = pop.model1)

COV.1000 is then a list of sample covariance matrices, with length == length(seeds).  You  can easily change the use of lapply() to mclapply() or parLapply().  Then you could write another function that accepts a single sample covariance matrix, analyzes it, and returns the output of interest.  In that case, COV.1000 is your "list" to apply that function to.

analyzeData <- function(x, N, mod) {
  fit <- lavaan(model = mod, sample.cov = x, sample.nobs = N, ...)
  lavInspect(fit, what = "whatever you want")
}

analysisModel <- ""
output <- lapply(COV.1000, analyzeData, N = 1000, mod = analysisModel)

Terry
